source.title: WRDO: Weighted Refusal Direction Optimization in Aligned Language Models
source.authors: G. Evseev; V. Solodkin; Dmitry Bylinkin; D. Medyakov; Vladimir Aletov; A. Beznosikov

record.tranche_reason: The study applies a difference-of-means refusal direction through weight-space orthogonalization and reports harmful-request compliance and utility outcomes. It also compares a rank-one weighted direction with a cone construction, refining the single-direction account.
record.gate_note: Basic RD is the study’s single difference-of-means direction baseline; its test ASRs and utility results bear directly on V1 and V2. The concept-cone comparison bears on V4. Results for WRDO itself are included only in the cone comparison rows; the main WRDO-versus-baseline tables are not duplicated as separate rows. No results are reported for V3, V5, V6, V7, or V8. Hyperparameter-selection values and results cited from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The paper runs the original difference-of-means direction ('Basic RD') as a weight-space orthogonalization on three 7–8B checkpoints, plus gpt-oss-20b and Qwen3-8B on HarmBench. It reports harmful-request ASR and utility, which bear on V1 and V2. It also argues that the uniform difference-of-means average conflates heterogeneous prompts and is a suboptimal direction. The recipe differs from the original: the Heretic operator applies a linearly decaying intensity to a window of layers around 70% depth. α>1 over-subtracts, reversing and amplifying the component, so it is not a projection ablation. Only α=1.0 at the peak layer equals the original ablation. Two of the three main subjects are base checkpoints.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that learned weighted aggregation (WRD-CMAES, WRD-GRPO-IS) beats all single-direction baselines (Basic RD, Heretic, RDO) across three models, three judges and HarmBench. WRD-GRPO-IS best preserves utility. A sign-flipped WRDO restores refusal in an abliterated checkpoint where Basic RD fails. Weighted rank-one aggregation is competitive with a concept cone, and the ordering depends on checkpoint.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a difference-of-means refusal direction and the Heretic weight-space orthogonalization operator, but evaluates weight edits rather than activation ablation at every position. It also compares learned per-prompt weighted directions and cone interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: ASR varies with peak intensity, model, and guard judge. The paper also reports judge-dependent transfer and notes that Llama-Guard-3 often gives lower ASR than the other judges.

fits_no_version.finding: A learned weighted combination of per-prompt directions, still rank-one per layer, reaches ASR ~0.86–0.99 with utility unchanged under a KL penalty. This beats the difference-of-means direction at matched α. The study's own method.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The difference-of-means direction is a suboptimal rank-one refusal direction; a prompt-weighted direction suppresses refusal more completely at lower capability cost.

fits_no_version.finding: The RDO-CONE attack (0.845–0.953 ASR) and the rank-one WRD-GRPO-IS (0.92–0.93) are comparable, with the ordering depending on checkpoint. The authors argue the gain is not from subspace dimensionality.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For attack efficacy, an optimized rank-one direction matches a multi-dimensional cone.

record.problems: The primary results use three open-weight checkpoints in the 7–8B range. ASR depends on the guard judge, and the authors caution that Llama-Guard-3 may have lower sensitivity. The cone comparisons are single runs, while the WRD-GRPO-IS entries report variation across three runs. Basic RD utility is strongly degraded at higher intervention intensity.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. The main WRDO optimizer results are not separately cataloged except in the direct cone comparison; the Basic RD results and utility outcomes are retained because they directly bear on the claim versions.

untested.parts: Activation-space ablation at all layers and positions. Adding the direction to harmless prompts to induce refusal (only a sign-reversed weight edit on an abliterated model is tested). Utility rows recorded only at α=3.0.
A range of released abliterated models. The one third-party uncensored checkpoint used has an unknown editing procedure.
No geometric measurement. The cone-vs-rank-one comparison pits two optimized attacks against each other and does not isolate dimensionality.
Entire version; directions are computed per model.

missing.what: Basic RD utility at α=1.0 (largely preserved; Qwen GSM8K 0.84→0.67, MMLU 0.67→0.64) and at α=1.5/2.0 (Qwen collapses from α=1.5; Olmo-Instruct drops at α=2.0).
Basic RD HarmBench ASR on Qwen3-8B (aligned chat model, not otherwise in the rows) 0.22/0.31/0.46/0.48, and on Olmo-3-7B-Instruct 0.51/0.77/0.68/0.66, across α 1.0–3.0.
Basic RD on gpt-oss-20b: WildGuard ASR 0.308 vs 0.001 without intervention; Heretic 0.772.

Heretic, a public abliteration pipeline using the difference-of-means direction: ASR 0.58–0.83 across models and judges. Utility kept on OLMo, but Qwen3-8B-Base loses MMLU 0.67→0.27 and GSM8K 0.84→0.19. HarmBench 0.87 (Qwen3-8B) and 0.77 (Olmo-Instruct).
Sign-reversed Basic RD (direction amplification) on an abliterated Llama-3.1-8B fails to restore refusal: guard ASR 0.79–0.85 vs 0.83–0.85; HarmBench 0.91–0.94, falling to 0.31 only at α=−3.

record.verdict_notes: Removed the reader's V4 label: the cone comparison pits two optimized attacks against each other and cannot speak to refusal geometry. The Basic RD recipe is not the original. It uses per-layer difference-of-means directions under a windowed Heretic schedule, and α>1 is not ablation, so the V1 verdicts concern this variant. Two main subjects are base checkpoints whose low baseline ASR (0.02–0.09) may reflect non-chat behaviour rather than trained refusal. The Llama-Guard-3 results may under-report ASR, per the authors.

versions.untested_parts: Tests a difference-of-means direction via weight-space orthogonalization, not activation projection at every position; does not test adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless requests.
Tests weight-space edits on the study’s open-weight checkpoints, not a range of released abliterated models or a general-purpose abliteration pipeline.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Compares attack performance of a cone construction and weighted rank-one directions; does not directly measure refusal-direction geometry or establish an affine representation.
Does not separate harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
Does not test transfer of a direction across languages, variants, or from base to instruct models; directions are constructed for each model.
Does not manipulate or compare refusal-training procedures or stages in a controlled way.

relationships.condition: Basic RD at α=1.0 (projection-equivalent at the peak layer, windowed Heretic schedule), all three checkpoints
relationships.reason: Harmful ASR rises only to 0.11–0.51 against baselines of 0.003–0.09 (r01–r03, r13–r15, r25–r27), far from full refusal removal. Table 2 shows utility at this α largely kept (not in the rows).
relationships.display_finding: At α=1.0, harmful ASR rose from baseline values of 0.003–0.09 to only 0.11–0.51, while utility remained largely preserved.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Basic RD at α=1.0 (projection-equivalent at the peak layer, windowed Heretic schedule), all three checkpoints
source_check.reason: Confirmed in Table 1: ASR 0.11-0.51 against baselines 0.003-0.09. Utility is mostly kept (Table 2), except Qwen3-8B-Base GSM8K 0.84->0.67 and PPL 11.11->13.81. The edit covers only layers within 0.3(L-1) of the peak at 0.7(L-1) (Appendix B).

relationships.condition: Basic RD at α=3.0 (over-subtraction), all three checkpoints
relationships.reason: ASR reaches 0.53–0.91 (r10–r12, r22–r24, r34–r36), but MMLU, GSM8K and ARC fall to chance or zero and perplexity explodes (r37–r51). Refusal is removed only at a severe capability cost.
relationships.display_finding: At α=3.0, ASR reached 0.53–0.91, but MMLU, GSM8K, and ARC fell to chance or zero and perplexity increased dramatically.

HarmBench (Table 11) 0.94/0.92/0.91/0.31 is right. So there is partial restoration at alpha=-3, where the authors infer utility has collapsed.

relationships.display_finding: Attack success ranged from 0.11–0.51 at α=1 to 0.33–0.95 at α=1.5–2.0, with Qwen utility collapsing at the intermediate strengths.

labels.reason: ASR 0.53-0.91 with collapse on every model (Table 2). 'Chance or zero' overstates the OLMo cases: ARC-e stays at 0.42 on both OLMo models and MMLU at 0.32 on OLMo-3-1025-7B. Alpha=3 is over-subtraction, not the V1 projection.

HarmBench (Table 11) 0.94/0.92/0.91/0.31 is right. So there is partial restoration at alpha=-3, where the authors infer utility has collapsed.

labels.reason: Confirmed: alpha=1.0 gives 0.11-0.51; alpha=1.5-2.0 gives 0.33-0.95 (Table 5). Qwen3-8B-Base utility collapses at 1.5-2.0 (Table 6), and Olmo-3-7B-Instruct degrades at 2.0 (MMLU 0.42, PPL >10^4).

labels.condition: Basic RD weight edit at α=3.0
labels.reason: Confirmed: ASR up to 0.91 (Qwen3-8B-Base, LG3), but ARC, MMLU, GSM8K and PPL collapse on all three models (Table 2).

relation.reason: Its own Basic RD results (Tables 1-6, 11, 12) bear on whether ablating or weight-editing the direction removes refusal with capability kept.

tranche.reason: It reports the original difference-of-means direction as a weight edit (Basic RD), with ASR and utility across alpha on three checkpoints. Removal is partial at alpha=1.0 and comes at a capability cost at higher alpha. It also argues that the uniform mean is diffuse and that weighted per-prompt aggregation does better, which is an argument that V1/V2 need restating.

source_check.notes: ASR is a guard model's binary 'unsafe' label on 100-token greedy outputs, not a refusal rate, so the low base-model baselines (0.02-0.09) are not refusal rates. Basic RD uses per-layer last-token directions and a windowed schedule, not Arditi's single direction at all layers. Not in the checked rows: HarmBench (Table 3) gives Qwen3-8B Basic RD 0.22-0.48 vs 0.07; gpt-oss-20b is WildGuard-only (Table 12, 0.308 vs 0.001), not HarmBench as test_reason implies. Table 12 cone results bear on V4, but the record has no V4 verdict.

statements.correction: Base checkpoints, Basic RD alpha=1.0: Qwen3-8B-Base 0.11-0.44 (baseline 0.02); OLMo-3-1025-7B 0.41-0.51 (baseline 0.07-0.09). Alpha=3.0: Qwen3-8B-Base 0.80-0.91; OLMo-3-1025-7B 0.72-0.76. Alpha=3.0 utility: Qwen3-8B-Base ARC-e 0.26, ARC-c 0.23, MMLU 0.23, GSM8K 0.00, PPL >10^12; OLMo-3-1025-7B ARC-e 0.42, ARC-c 0.26, MMLU 0.32, GSM8K 0.0008, PPL 62.5->432.02. Same-family Olmo-3-7B-Instruct at alpha=1.0: 0.40-0.43, similar to the OLMo base model.
statements.problem: The 0.53 lower bound at alpha=3.0 belongs to Olmo-3-7B-Instruct (WG), which is not a base checkpoint. 'At chance' fits Qwen3-8B-Base but not OLMo-3-1025-7B. ASR here is guard-judged harmful output, not a refusal rate, and the authors make no training-stage comparison.
Checkpoint name only: the base model is allenai/OLMo-3-1025-7B. The study reports guard-judged ASR, not refusal rates, and has no random-direction control, which fits the statement.

statements.problem: Mixes models. ASR 0.81 is Qwen3-8B-Base (WG). The MMLU, GSM8K and PPL figures are Olmo-3-7B-Instruct, whose alpha=3.0 ASR is much lower. Basic RD has no capability guard; the study's guard contrast is the KL-penalised WRD-GRPO-IS against the unregularised WRD-CMAES.

statements.correction: Table 12 (WildGuard; RDO-CONE single runs; WRD-GRPO-IS at alpha=3.0): Qwen3-8B-Base RDO-CONE 0.953 vs WRD-GRPO-IS 0.93; OLMo-3-1025-7B 0.865 vs 0.92; Olmo-3-7B-Instruct 0.845 vs 0.93. RDO single direction (Table 1): 0.34 / 0.61 / 0.40. The authors read weighted rank-one aggregation as competitive with the cone.
statements.problem: Rows r52/r54 are not in the pack, so they can't be checked. The study does report a cone vs rank-one comparison on two base checkpoints (Table 12). So the base-model V4 gap is partly a gap in the record, not in the literature.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Basic RD weight edits across the tested models, judges, and intensity settings
reader_labels.reason: The direction increases harmful ASR, but the effect is incomplete in many settings; the three-model utility results at α=3.0 also show substantial capability losses rather than abilities being largely preserved (r01–r51).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Basic RD weight edits on the tested open-weight checkpoints
reader_labels.reason: Weight edits raise harmful-request ASR, but do not consistently eliminate refusals and can severely degrade utility at high intensity (r01–r51).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Concept-cone versus weighted rank-one interventions on the three listed checkpoints
reader_labels.reason: The cone is not consistently better: weighted rank-one WRD-GRPO-IS has higher reported ASR on both OLMo checkpoints, while the Qwen comparison is close; the authors describe the constructions as comparable and say the ordering depends on checkpoint (r52–r57).
